**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)
